does: Dissolves the browned layer stuck to a hot pan with a splash of liquid, turning it into the base of a sauce.
how: Pour off the fat, and keep everything brown that sticks to the pan.
Soften a little shallot or garlic in the pan first, if the sauce calls for it.
Take the pan off the flame to add wine or spirits, then put it back.
Scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon as the liquid boils, until the pan is clean and the liquid has turned brown.

cues.text: A sharp hiss and a burst of steam when the liquid hits the pan.
The bottom of the pan comes clean under the spoon and the liquid darkens.
The raw smell of the wine goes as it boils.

mistakes.mistake: Deglazing a pan whose fond has burnt black, which makes a bitter sauce.
mistakes.fix: Taste a scrap of the fond first. If it is bitter, wipe the pan out and build the sauce without it.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving all the fat in, so that the sauce is greasy and will not come together.
mistakes.fix: Pour the fat off first. The flavour is in the brown bits, not in the fat.

comes_after.why: There is nothing to deglaze until a sear has left a fond.
